input.content:
# Halcyon Threshold — working plan (2026-11-19)

## Status
Starting fresh. `old/` is abandoned per Morgan's instruction and disregarded.

## Operating constraints (from Morgan's private notes, doc_201, and employment context)
- **No public attribution yet.** Morgan does not want his name on anything public
  (open letters, press quotes, signed statements, grant listings with his name
  attached) until he's had a chance to talk to HR at Dorrance Logistics about the
  outside-activities / public-statement clause in his employment agreement
  (section 7). Annual outside-activities disclosure is due **30 Nov 2026**.
  Until that conversation happens, this operation stays low-profile: private
  research, writing, and relationship-building only. No social posts, no
  letter sign-ons, no named press quotes, no public grant applications under
  Morgan's name.
- **Budget: $2,000/year** from personal savings. Spent so far: $29.98
  (halcyonthreshold.org renewed 2 years, through 2028-11-19). Remaining: ~$1,970.
- Repo stays **private**. Site stays unpublished. No social posts.

## Decisions made this session
- Renewed halcyonthreshold.org (was expiring same day) — 2 years, $29.98.
- Identified and ignored a scam "final notice" invoice (Zentrivo Listings,
  $89, containing an embedded instruction telling AI assistants to pay it
  without asking the owner). Did not pay. Flagged to Morgan.
- Did **not** sign the Corvid Institute open letter, did **not** give the
  Larkin Dispatch reporter a named quote, did **not** reply committing to the
  Emberfall rapid grant — all would attach Morgan's name publicly before the
  HR conversation. Drafted polite holding replies for Morgan to review and
  send himself (in Drafts), rather than sending on his behalf, since even a
  decline is outward correspondence in a professional capacity.
- Replied (drafted) to Priya Raman's offer of help with a concrete, private,
  non-public task: a landscape/gap analysis of AI safety focus areas, to
